leads.work: Logistics asked again and again to create or extend Sitara deal tickets for meters where gas flowed with no deal. This covers small or trickle volumes, days after a deal ended, month rollovers, and volumes parked on the Strangers Gas contract.
leads.why: Volume management (Aimee Lannou, Ricky Ellis, Mary Poorman, Jackie Young, Clem Cernosek, Thu Nguyen) sends Daren Farmer one-off requests nearly every week, each citing the last deal number. Clem's form asks either for a deal or for approval to write off 203 MMBtu spread over 19 months. These look rule-based and could be automated, for example auto-extending the prior month's deal or setting a write-off threshold.

leads.work: Researching customer billing disputes and missing or mispriced deals. A customer says a spot deal was done or invoiced differently, and several people search deal sheets, Sitara and Path Manager to confirm.
leads.why: The CP&L Feb 21 dispute ran through 7+ emails and five people over a $405 difference, and CP&L later raised another request to add deals. Other cases: Conoco called twice about a missing 5/5 sale; a PG&E Texas invoice had no deal in Unify; the LCRA price showed $2.50 against $4.50; Karen Lindley needed a deal number; an O'Connor flash had no matching Unify record. The root cause is spot deals not being captured at the time of trade.

leads.work: Clearing feedback-monitor and bridge errors for old production months, where POPS, MOPS and Sitara disagree and a deal ticket or allocation must be fixed.
leads.why: A single January 1999 error at meter 984132 bounced between Karen Lindley, Jackie Young, Gary Lamphier and Daren Farmer for two weeks (8/21 to 9/5), with heavily duplicated forwards. Separate bridge errors on transport tickets also had to be watched by hand. This points to a reconciliation gap between the systems.

leads.work: Updating Sitara deal prices and demand charges by hand to match actual pipeline statements so that settlements can redraft invoices. This includes monthly 'please update and let me know when done' loops.
leads.why: Each month Audrey Cook and Kevin Drachenberg ask Giron to update Peoples/North Shore transport demand charges (#131389, #131405). One fuel adjustment took from March to August. Megan Parker asked for a plug fixed price, and Jane Saladino reported the same OA pricing difference recurring every month after SAP removed netting.

leads.work: Tracking unfinaled sales and purchase invoices on monthly spreadsheets sent to each department, with deadlines to clear them.
leads.why: Lisa Csikos sends spreadsheets every month assigning a 'Responsible Department' to each item, for May production and earlier, and purchases follow the next week. This is recurring manual chasing.

leads.work: Monthly and quarterly volume-variance explanations for Investor Relations: explaining every change of more than 10% year/year, quarter/quarter and month/month.
leads.why: Misti Day: "It's that time again for the monthly and quarterly volumetric explanations". The request recurs, and commercial staff must verify the numbers.

leads.work: Monthly hours survey and activity-driver survey for cost allocation (Operations Pricing Model).
leads.why: The surveys go to 50+ managers each month. Shari Mao herself suggests sending existing standard reports instead to 'eliminate your need to fill out this survey every month.' The survey was paused for redesign in July and August.

leads.work: Semi-annual PRC (performance review) process: gathering accomplishments lists, confirming reviewer feedback and rosters, and holding day-long committee meetings.
leads.why: Every six months: requests for accomplishments, the HR roster check, a feedback request for Audrey Cook, and a long agenda email with a template. All of it is manual email collection.

leads.work: Setting up new trading books or portfolios across Tagg, Sitara, Global Counterparty and EOL, which needs separate requests to different groups plus pipe and curve mapping.
leads.why: Splitting Midcon into two books meant emails to Imelda Frayre, Ron Nolte, Gary Stadler, GCP and EOL (Stephanie Sever). Giron forwarded the thread to show how long it took (about two weeks). More books followed in August, and book lists were sent to several people by hand.

leads.work: Daily reconciliation of origination amounts recognized on desk P&L against the origination schedule.
leads.why: Gabriel Monroy, Binh Pham and Rahmaan Mwongozi send nightly emails about small differences ($468, $771, $11,812) that Giron then forwards to staff to research.

leads.work: Daily P&L and DPR distribution for EMW/Enovate: approval emails, reissuing corrected versions, and requesting unprotected copies so they can be forwarded.
leads.why: Recurring requests to Daniel Falcone for printable or forwardable DPR copies, plus a resend after confusion over which P&L version had been signed off.

leads.work: Booking EOL deals into both Tagg and Sitara by hand: linking deal numbers, rebooking failed EOL deals, rebooking EOL park-and-loan deals as four Sitara deals, and fixing EOL deals changed or booked to the wrong counterparty.
leads.why: Giron's procedures list several manual cross-references to make 'on each and every deal'. Other evidence: an EOL park-and-loan deal rebooked by hand; Pat Clynes' repeated reminders that EOL deals must not be changed; an Aquila deal changed; Southern Co. paths redone; a Dynegy counterparty fix in Tagg.

leads.work: Customer and affiliate nominations arriving as emailed Word or Excel attachments that are re-keyed into deals and noms (Calpine daily and monthly, Enron Methanol/MTBE monthly, Eastrans/Duke, Reliant, Midlothian forecast, Prize revised noms).
leads.why: The same senders send nominations by email every day or month as attachments. Daren adjusts deals by hand from them (for example, adding 5,000 of swing for Methanol).

leads.work: Reporting pipeline cuts and imbalances by email (Oasis/El Paso cuts, Oasis contract imbalances), plus written cut-handling procedures.
leads.why: Mark McCoy sends repeated FYI lists of cuts and imbalance updates. Bill Williams has a written cut procedure stressing 'document everything'. Cut data could be captured in a structured way.

leads.work: Notices of meter shut-ins, pigging and maintenance outages, forwarded and re-forwarded to Contracts, Logistics and Producer Services, plus producer letter requests.
leads.why: Gary Hanks sends repeated distribution emails (Baytown pigging announced, cancelled, then rescheduled three times; Wilson Creek; Shawnee; McMullen) to the same list. Contracts replies to check whether any contract is affected.

leads.work: Weekend on-call notes summarizing nominations, cuts and meter issues for the Monday team.
leads.why: Recurring weekly free-text notes sent to the whole logistics list.

leads.work: Reconciling flash estimates to actuals (fuel on third-party pipes, July flash-to-actual for EMW).
leads.why: The fuel flash was 24,302 MMBtu but actuals came in at 12,511, which set off a chain of 'where did we miss' emails. Separate flash-to-actual meetings also took place. Shipper-paid fuel cannot be handled in Sitara, Brenda Herod was told Steve called it 'a nightmare', and Michael Eiben said the process was not in place.

leads.work: Monthly setup of transport usage tickets, where baseload rates must be adjusted by hand once traders agree them.
leads.why: Heidi Withers updates the tickets each month and asks traders to adjust rates and report the agreed rates back.

leads.work: Allocation and accounting-arrangement corrections in POPS/Unify for specific contracts (CILCO, meter 692, Equistar and Formosa buyback tickets, Teco tailgate adjustment).
leads.why: The CILCO issues are described as 'so many... I'm not sure which one'. Buyback tickets are needed every month before an invoice can be drafted, and the Formosa deal expired with no replacement. The Teco adjustment has run monthly for 5 years without a written agreement, which keeps causing Sitara/Unify problems.

leads.work: Deals on an inactive desk (ECT-IM Waha) that keep rolling because of the evergreen flag and must be converted by hand.
leads.why: Thomas Engel flagged deals that should have ended; Daren asked whether they could be changed systematically.

leads.work: Handling parking and loan transactions with a multi-step manual booking procedure (a storage deal, two exchange deals, and swaps).
leads.why: The procedure is complex and error-prone, and prior-period imbalances need case-by-case decisions.

leads.work: New-hire system access requests submitted application by application (CPR, Sitara, Unify, Lotus Notes).
leads.why: Each access request goes through the SRRS email loop.

leads.work: Confirming HL&P special-deal volumes and monthly volume spreadsheets.
leads.why: Ed Gottlob notes the HL&P dealmaker keeps calling to get volumes, so they must be agreed by hand before billing.

leads.work: Reviewing reports and product setups (Desk Summary report in CPR, hourly gas deal positions, new EOL hourly or flexible products that need a new GTC).
leads.why: Each new product type needs a manual process across legal, Sitara and logistics. Report upgrade reviews also recur.

leads.work: Organizing customer events (customer trip, happy hours) and rescheduling them.
leads.why: Admin time on RSVP tracking, follow-up calls and rescheduling.
